# Garage AI

> Garage AI (GarageAI) is a two-sided marketplace for local AI inference in Europe. Garage owners ("operators") connect GPUs they already own and get paid per token for the requests they serve; buyers use open models through one OpenAI-compatible API. The principle: Europe's AI capacity can come from hardware people and companies already own, not only from hyperscaler data centres.

## Key facts (what works today)

- **For buyers:** Sign up at https://app.garageai.eu, create an API key and call the OpenAI-compatible API at https://llm.garageai.eu/v1 (works with OpenAI SDKs, agents and coding tools), or use the chat in the portal. Pay per token with prepaid credits (card via Stripe).
- **Two ways to buy a model:** "Pool" (cheaper, load-balanced across every garage offering the model, automatic failover) or "Specific garage" (a named garage, e.g. for location; shared, not exclusive capacity).
- **For operators:** Sign up at https://app.garageai.eu/auth?intent=operator and follow the "Offer your GPU" wizard. Supported OS: macOS and Linux (not Windows yet). Supported runtimes: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM. One command installs the NetBird client, joins the encrypted mesh and registers the models. Every model must pass an automated acceptance test (time-to-first-token, tokens/second) before it can be sold.
- **Operator earnings:** Operators earn the token price buyers pay for requests their garage serves. No platform fee during launch (a fee will come later). Wallet and payouts are being built.
- **Technology (open source):** Self-hosted NetBird (WireGuard mesh) — no inbound ports, garages cannot reach each other, only the gateway reaches a runtime. LiteLLM gateway (OpenAI-compatible API, routing, failover, usage metering) on an EU VPS (Hetzner, Helsinki).
- **Privacy, honestly:** Traffic is encrypted in transit over the mesh, but prompts are processed on the operator's machine. Verified garages and data-processing agreements are planned before selling to buyers with sensitive data.
- **Status:** Live, with the first garages serving open models.
- **License:** Open source, MIT.

## Vision (not today's product)

Garage nodes running largely on locally produced energy (rooftop solar, home batteries, EV batteries), many more garages across Europe, and larger regional clusters.
